title: Forklift fuel, batteries, lighting and loading docks practice questions
description: Practice questions on forklift fuel storage, battery charging, lighting, carbon monoxide, dockboards, trucks and railroad cars (29 CFR 1910.178(f)-(k)).

questions.question: A plant stores diesel fuel for its trucks. Under 1910.178(f)(1), the storage and handling shall be in accordance with which code?

options.A: NFPA Storage and Handling of Liquefied Petroleum Gases (NFPA No. 58-1969)
options.B: NFPA Flammable and Combustible Liquids Code (NFPA No. 30-1969)
options.C: The levels specified in § 1910.1000
options.D: Subpart D of this part

questions.explanation: 1910.178(f)(1) says "The storage and handling of liquid fuels such as gasoline and diesel fuel shall be in accordance with NFPA Flammable and Combustible Liquids Code (NFPA No. 30-1969)".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.178(f)(2), the storage and handling of which fuel shall be in accordance with NFPA No. 58-1969?

options.A: Gasoline
options.B: Diesel fuel
options.C: Battery electrolyte
options.D: Liquefied petroleum gas fuel

questions.explanation: 1910.178(f)(2) says "The storage and handling of liquefied petroleum gas fuel shall be in accordance with NFPA Storage and Handling of Liquefied Petroleum Gases (NFPA No. 58-1969)".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Where does 1910.178(g)(1) say battery charging installations shall be located?

options.A: In areas designated for that purpose
options.B: Outdoors only
options.C: Next to the liquid fuel storage area
options.D: In the same room as the truck repair shop

questions.explanation: 1910.178(g)(1) says "Battery charging installations shall be located in areas designated for that purpose."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Electrolyte spills on the floor of a battery charging installation. Which facility does 1910.178(g)(2) say shall be provided for that situation?

options.A: A floor drain leading to the storm sewer
options.B: A fan to dry the floor
options.C: Facilities for flushing and neutralizing spilled electrolyte
options.D: An open bin of sawdust beside each charger

questions.explanation: 1910.178(g)(2) says "Facilities shall be provided for flushing and neutralizing spilled electrolyte", along with the other facilities it lists.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A battery charging area sits beside a busy truck aisle. Which facility listed in 1910.178(g)(2) deals with the trucks themselves?

options.A: A posted speed limit for the aisle
options.B: Convex mirrors at each corner of the area
options.C: Facilities for protecting charging apparatus from damage by trucks
options.D: A traffic signal at the area's entrance

questions.explanation: 1910.178(g)(2) says facilities shall be provided "for protecting charging apparatus from damage by trucks", along with the other facilities it lists.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A plant sets up a battery charging installation with facilities for flushing and neutralizing spilled electrolyte, barriers that protect the chargers from trucks, and ventilation for battery fumes. It decides fire protection is unnecessary because no fuel is stored nearby. What does 1910.178(g)(2) say?

options.A: Facilities for fire protection shall be provided too; (g)(2) makes no exception for areas without fuel
options.B: The plant is right; fire protection is needed only where fuel is stored
options.C: Fire protection is needed only if batteries are charged overnight
options.D: Fire protection is needed only if more than one charger is installed

questions.explanation: 1910.178(g)(2) says "Facilities shall be provided for flushing and neutralizing spilled electrolyte, for fire protection, for protecting charging apparatus from damage by trucks, and for adequate ventilation for dispersal of fumes from gassing batteries." It sets no condition on the fire protection facilities.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A maintenance worker plans to cut a steel bracket with an angle grinder, which throws sparks, inside a battery charging area. What does 1910.178(g)(11) require?

options.A: Nothing, because the rule covers only smoking
options.B: Nothing, as long as the battery covers are closed
options.C: Nothing, once the area's ventilation is switched on
options.D: Precautions shall be taken to prevent sparks in the battery charging area

questions.explanation: 1910.178(g)(11) says "Precautions shall be taken to prevent open flames, sparks, or electric arcs in battery charging areas." Sparks from a grinder fall under that requirement.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A mechanic is working near a battery whose top is uncovered. What does 1910.178(g)(12) say about tools and other metallic objects?

options.A: They shall be wrapped in insulating tape
options.B: They shall be kept away from the top of uncovered batteries
options.C: They shall be grounded before use
options.D: They shall be stored in a locked cabinet inside the charging area

questions.explanation: 1910.178(g)(12) says "Tools and other metallic objects shall be kept away from the top of uncovered batteries."

questions.question: What does 1910.178(g)(4) say shall be provided for handling batteries?

options.A: A conveyor, overhead hoist, or equivalent material handling equipment
options.B: A carboy tilter or siphon
options.C: Two employees for every battery lift
options.D: Lifting straps worn by the employee

questions.explanation: 1910.178(g)(4) says "A conveyor, overhead hoist, or equivalent material handling equipment shall be provided for handling batteries."

questions.question: Which equipment does 1910.178(g)(6) say shall be provided for handling electrolyte?

options.A: An overhead hoist
options.B: A pressurized spray nozzle
options.C: A carboy tilter or siphon
options.D: An open bucket and funnel

questions.explanation: 1910.178(g)(6) says "A carboy tilter or siphon shall be provided for handling electrolyte."

questions.question: 1910.178(g)(7) sets the order in which acid and water are combined. During which activity does it apply?

options.A: When cleaning trucks
options.B: When charging batteries
options.C: When filling water mufflers
options.D: When disposing of a used battery

questions.explanation: 1910.178(g)(7) says "When charging batteries, acid shall be poured into water; water shall not be poured into acid."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A battery that was taken out is being put back into the truck. What does 1910.178(g)(5) require?

options.A: It shall be fully charged before it is reinstalled
options.B: It shall be reinstalled with its cover closed and locked
options.C: It shall be reinstalled only by a licensed electrician
options.D: It shall be properly positioned and secured in the truck

questions.explanation: 1910.178(g)(5) says "Reinstalled batteries shall be properly positioned and secured in the truck."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.178(g)(9) say about the battery (or compartment) cover(s)?

options.A: They shall be closed to keep out sparks
options.B: They shall be removed and stored outside the charging area
options.C: They shall be locked during charging
options.D: They shall be open to dissipate heat

questions.explanation: 1910.178(g)(9) says "The battery (or compartment) cover(s) shall be open to dissipate heat."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.178(g)(9), care shall be taken to assure what about vent caps?

options.A: That they are functioning
options.B: That they are removed before charging
options.C: That they are sealed with tape
options.D: That they are replaced at every battery change

questions.explanation: 1910.178(g)(9) says "Care shall be taken to assure that vent caps are functioning."

questions.question: In an operating area, general lighting is less than 2 lumens per square foot. What does 1910.178(h)(2) require?

options.A: Truck operation shall stop until the lighting is improved
options.B: The operator shall travel in reverse
options.C: Auxiliary directional lighting shall be provided on the truck
options.D: A second employee shall walk ahead with a flashlight

questions.explanation: 1910.178(h)(2) says "Where general lighting is less than 2 lumens per square foot, auxiliary directional lighting shall be provided on the truck."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Gasoline trucks work inside a closed warehouse and carbon monoxide builds up in the air. Under 1910.178(i)(1), what sets the limit for the carbon monoxide concentration created by the truck operations?

options.A: A level chosen by the truck manufacturer
options.B: The levels specified in § 1910.1000
options.C: No limit applies as long as one door is kept open
options.D: Whatever level the operators report they can tolerate

questions.explanation: 1910.178(i)(1) says "Concentration levels of carbon monoxide gas created by powered industrial truck operations shall not exceed the levels specified in § 1910.1000."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Trucks operate in an area where general lighting measures 4 lumens per square foot. What does 1910.178(h)(2) require about auxiliary directional lighting on the trucks there?

options.A: (h)(2) does not require it there, because general lighting is not less than 2 lumens per square foot
options.B: Auxiliary directional lighting shall be provided on each truck
options.C: General lighting shall be raised to at least 10 lumens per square foot
options.D: Trucks shall operate there only in daylight hours

questions.explanation: 1910.178(h)(2) applies "Where general lighting is less than 2 lumens per square foot"; then "auxiliary directional lighting shall be provided on the truck." At 4 lumens per square foot that condition is not met.

questions.topic: Highway trucks, semitrailers and railroad cars
questions.question: Under 1910.178(k)(1), a highway truck's brakes are set and wheel chocks are placed under its rear wheels to keep it from rolling during which activity?

options.A: While its driver rests in the cab
options.B: While it is being fueled
options.C: While it travels on public roads
options.D: While it is boarded with powered industrial trucks

questions.explanation: 1910.178(k)(1) says "The brakes of highway trucks shall be set and wheel chocks placed under the rear wheels to prevent the trucks from rolling while they are boarded with powered industrial trucks."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Highway trucks, semitrailers and railroad cars
questions.question: A railroad car is being loaded at a siding that has no wheel stops. Which alternative to wheel stops does 1910.178(k)(2) name for preventing the car from moving during the loading?

options.A: A worker who watches the car
options.B: A painted stop line on the rail
options.C: Other recognized positive protection
options.D: A warning sign on the car

questions.explanation: 1910.178(k)(2) says "Wheel stops or other recognized positive protection shall be provided to prevent railroad cars from moving during loading or unloading operations."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Highway trucks, semitrailers and railroad cars
questions.question: 1910.178(k)(3) says fixed jacks may be necessary to support a semitrailer. Which hazard does it name them as preventing?

options.A: The trailer's tires going flat
options.B: Upending during the loading or unloading
options.C: The dockboard sliding off the trailer
options.D: Theft of the trailer

questions.explanation: 1910.178(k)(3) says "Fixed jacks may be necessary to support a semitrailer and prevent upending during the loading or unloading when the trailer is not coupled to a tractor."
